title: Clustered Indexes
description: Learn how clustered indexes organize data physically and how they relate to primary keys.

data.text: A clustered index stores data rows in a sorted structure based on its key values. Each table has only one clustered index because data rows can be only sorted in one order. A table that has a clustered index is called a clustered table.

data.alt: B-tree structure of a clustered index

data.text: A clustered index organizes data using a B-tree (balanced tree) structure which enables searches, inserts, updates, and deletes in logarithmic amortized time.
When you create a table with a primary key, SQL Server automatically creates a corresponding clustered index that includes the primary key columns.

data.title: Create Table with Primary Key
data.content: Creates a table with a primary key that automatically creates a clustered index.

data.text: If a table does not have a primary key, you can use the CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX statement to add a clustered index:

data.title: CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX
data.content: Creates a clustered index on the part_id column.
data.code:
CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX ix_parts_id
ON production.parts (part_id);

data.text: A table without a clustered index is a heap: rows have no defined order and are located through a row identifier (RID). Adding a clustered index turns the table into a B-tree that stores the actual rows at the leaf level, sorted by the key. The script below builds one of each and compares the metadata.

data.title: Create a heap, then add a clustered index
data.content: The `type_desc` column reads HEAP first and CLUSTERED after the index is created.

data.title: Keys are copied everywhere
data.text: Non-clustered indexes on a clustered table store the clustered key as their row locator, so a wide clustered key (for example a random GUID or a long composite key) makes every non-clustered index wider and slows inserts. Keep the clustered key narrow, unique, and ever-increasing — an IDENTITY int or bigint is ideal.

data.title: Clustered Index Key Points
points: A clustered index physically organizes data in a table according to the index key.
When creating a table with a primary key, SQL Server automatically creates a clustered index.
A table has only one clustered index.
Use CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX to add a clustered index to a table without a primary key.
